questions.question: The ratio of the present age of Mitali to that of Shabnam is 4 : 7. If the difference between the present age of Shabnam and the age of Mitali after 5 years will be 13 years, then what is the sum of the present ages of Mitali and shabnam?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the present age of Mitali to that of Shabnam is 4 : 7. If the difference between the present age of Shabnam and the age of Mitali after 5 years will be 13 years, then what is the sum of the present ages of Mitali and shabnam?
questions.solution:
Let the present age of Mitali and Shabnam be 4x and 7x.

Mitali’s age after 5 years will be 4x + 5,

The difference between present age of Shabnam and Mitali’s age after 5 years = 7x - (4x + 5) = 13

7x - 4x - 5 = 13

3x = 13 + 5

3x = 18

x = 6

Hence present ages of Mitali and Shabnam will be 24 and 42.

Sum of the present age of Mitali and Shabnam = 24 + 42 = 66

Hence, 66 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which two signs should be changed in the following equation to make it correct? 9 - 3 + 12 × 8 ÷ 4 = 11
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs should be changed in the following equation to make it correct?

9 - 3 + 12 × 8 ÷ 4 = 11
questions.solution:
Given equation: 9 - 3 + 12 × 8 ÷ 4  = 11

1) Interchanging - and ÷

9 ÷ 3 + 12 × 8 - 4

= 3 + 96 - 4

= 99 - 4 = 95 ≠ 11

2) Interchanging + and ÷

9 - 3 ÷ 12 × 8 + 4

= 9 - 0.25 × 8 + 4

= 11

3) Interchanging + and -

9 + 3 - 12 × 8 ÷ 4

= 12 - 24

= - 12 ≠ 11

4) Interchanging × and +

9 - 3 × 12 + 8 ÷  4

= 9 - 36 + 8 ÷ 4

= 11 - 36

= -25 ≠ 11

Hence, by interchanging ÷ and + we get the correct equation.

questions.question: A person sold 25 articles for Rs. 2500 and incurred a loss of 10%. How many articles should he sell for Rs. 2400 to make a profit of 20%?
questions.questionHtml: A person sold 25 articles for Rs. 2500 and incurred a loss of 10%. How many articles should he sell for Rs. 2400 to make a profit of 20%?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the direct relation: (Total Price1 / (Quantity1 × (100 − Loss%))) = (Total Price2 / (Quantity2 × (100 + Profit%)))

⇒ 2500 / (25 × 90) = 2400 / (n × 120)

⇒ 100 / 90 = 20 / n

⇒ 10 / 9 = 20 / n

⇒ n = (20 × 9) / 10 = 18

∴ The correct answer is 18.

Alternate Method

Given:

Quantity1 = 25 articles, Total SP1 = ₹2500, Loss = 10%

Desired Profit = 20%, Total SP2 = ₹2400

Formula: Cost Price (CP) = (100 × SP) / (100 ± P/L%)

⇒ Selling Price (SP) of 1 article = 2500 ÷ 25 = ₹100

⇒ Since loss is 10%, 90% of CP = ₹100

⇒ CP of 1 article = 100 ÷ 0.9 = ₹1000/9

⇒ New SP required for 20% profit = 120% of CP

⇒ New SP = (120/100) × (1000/9) = ₹400/3

⇒ Number of articles for ₹2400 = Total SP ÷ New SP per article

⇒ Number of articles = 2400 ÷ (400/3) = (2400 × 3) ÷ 400 = 6 × 3 = 18

∴ The correct answer is 18.

Additional Information

Cost Price and Selling Price Relationship

Cost Price (CP) is always considered 100%. If there is a profit of P%, SP = (100 + P)% of CP. If there is a loss of L%, SP = (100 − L)% of CP.

Unitary Method in Profit and Loss

When the number of articles changes, it is easiest to find the CP or SP of one single unit before calculating the total for the new quantity.

Profit/Loss Percentage

questions.questionHtml: The area of a field in the shape of a triangle with each side x meters is equal to the area another triangular field having sides 50 m. 70 m and 80 m. The value of x is closed to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Area of triangle with sides 50, 70, 80: s = 100, Area = √(100 × 50 × 30 × 20) = 1000√3 m2.

Equilateral triangle area = (√3/4) × x2.

Equating both: (√3/4) × x2 = 1000√3 ⇒ x2 = 4000.

x = √4000 ≈ 63.24 m.

∴ The correct answer is 63.2 m.

Alternate Method

Given: Sides of the second triangular field are 50 m, 70 m, and 80 m. The first field is an equilateral triangle with side x.

Formula Used: Heron's formula Area = √(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)) and Equilateral Area = (√3/4)x2.

⇒ Semi-perimeter (s) = (50 + 70 + 80) / 2 = 100 m

⇒ Area of second field = √(100 × (100−50) × (100−70) × (100−80))

⇒ Area = √(100 × 50 × 30 × 20) = √(3,000,000) = 1000√3 m2

⇒ Area of first field = (√3 / 4) × x2 = 1000√3

⇒ x2 = 4000

⇒ x = √4000 = 20√10 ≈ 20 × 3.162 = 63.24 m

∴ The correct answer is 63.2 m.

Additional Information

Heron's Formula

Used for scalene triangles where sides a, b, c are known: Area = √(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)) where s = (a+b+c)/2.

Equilateral Triangle Properties

For side x, Area = (√3/4)x2 and Height = (√3/2)x.

Square Root Approximations

Since 602 = 3600 and 702 = 4900, √4000 must lie between 60 and 70, specifically closer to 63 (632 = 3969).

questions.question: A Person can row a distance of 4 km upstream in 1 hour 20 minutes and can row back to the starting point in just 24 minutes. How much time (in hours) will he take to row 13 km in still water?
questions.questionHtml: A Person can row a distance of 4 km upstream in 1 hour 20 minutes and can row back to the starting point in just 24 minutes. How much time (in hours) will he take to row 13 km in still water?
questions.solution:
Given:

Time taken to cover a distance of 4 km upstream = 1 hour 20 minutes = 4/3 hours

Time taken to cover a distance of 4 km downstream = 24 minutes

Concept Used:

The direction along the stream is called downstream.

The direction against the stream is called upstream.

Formula Used:

Distance = Speed × Times

Downstream speed of the boat = Speed of boat + Speed of stream

⇒ Ds = x + y

Upstream speed of the boat = Speed of boat - Speed of stream

⇒ Us = x - y

Calculation:

Let Speed of boat in still water be x km/hr & speed of stream be y km/hr

According to the question,

⇒ 4/(x – y) = 4/3

⇒ x – y = 3      ----(1)

⇒ 4/(x + y) = 24/60

⇒ x + y = 10     ----(2)

Add equation (1) and equation (2) we get,

⇒ 2x = 13

⇒ x = 13/2 km/hr

Time taken to row 13 km in still water = Distance covered/Speed of boat

Time taken = 13 ÷ 13/2 = 2 hrs

∴ The time taken to row 13 km in still water is 2 hours.

questions.question: To do a certain work, A and B work on alternate days, with B beginning the work on the first day. A can finish the work alone in 48 days. If the work gets completed in \(11\frac{1}{3}\) days, then B alone can finish 4 times the same work in:
questions.questionHtml: To do a certain work, A and B work on alternate days, with B beginning the work on the first day. A can finish the work alone in 48 days. If the work gets completed in \(11\frac{1}{3}\) days, then B alone can finish 4 times the same work in:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total time = 11(1/3) days (B starts first). B works on days 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 (6 days); A works on days 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 1/3 of day 12 (5 + 1/3 = 16/3 days).

Work done by A = (16/3) ÷ 48 = 1/9. Remaining work done by B = 1 − 1/9 = 8/9.

B finishes 8/9 work in 6 days ⇒ B finishes full work in (6 × 9)/8 = 27/4 days.

B finishes 4 times the work in (27/4) × 4 = 27 days.

∴ The correct answer is 27 days.

Alternate Method

Given: A alone = 48 days. Total alternate time = 11(1/3) days. B starts on day 1.

Distribution of work days:

⇒ B works on days: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 → Total 6 days.

⇒ A works on days: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 1/3 of the 12th day → Total 5 + 1/3 = 16/3 days.

⇒ Work done by A in 16/3 days = (16/3) × (1/48) = 1/9 of total work.

⇒ Work done by B in 6 days = 1 − 1/9 = 8/9 of total work.

⇒ Time taken by B to finish 1 complete work = 6 ÷ (8/9) = (6 × 9) / 8 = 27/4 days.

⇒ Time taken by B to finish 4 times the same work = 4 × (27/4) = 27 days.

∴ The correct answer is 27 days.

Additional Information

Alternate Day Work

In alternate work, identify who starts first. If total time is T, and B starts, B works for ceil(T/2) days if T is not an even integer and cycle is 2 days.

Efficiency and Time

Time is inversely proportional to Efficiency. Work = Efficiency × Time. For multiple works, New Time = Original Time × Multiplier.

questions.question: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. It has been a leading producer of both industrial and agricultural goods. B. questions.solution:

  • Sentence C links back to the high output mentioned in sentence A and further elaborates on its result, a major share in world trade.

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.
